title: reduce streaming token latency: token loop, flush cadence, backpressure, kv cache & kernel scheduling
author: Priya Shah
description: Summary: This PR reduces end-to-end streaming token generation latency by addressing multiple sources of per-token jitter and flush amplification across the serving runtime. Motivation: customers observed tail latency spikes and perceptible streaming lag during typical interactive workloads; root cause analysis showed small inefficiencies in the token emission loop, suboptimal flush cadence that interferes with batching, backpressure handling that introduced spin/wakeup cost, and KV-cache eviction/lookup hotspots that became visible under continuous batching. Changes: 1) reworked the token emission loop to avoid an extra scheduling hop per token and to batch flush decisions, 2) introduced an adaptive flush cadence that coalesces micro-flushes under high throughput while honoring latency SLOs, 3) added cooperative backpressure signaling to reduce kernel scheduler thrash and thread wakeups, 4) optimized KV-cache hot-path by adding a fast-path lookup and read-prefetch for the common case, 5) tuned kernel scheduling heuristics to prioritize lower-latency streams and avoid long-running kernel preemption, 6) added continuous-batcher tuning knobs and an auto-tuner that adjusts micro-batch sizes based on observed latency/throughput tradeoffs. Compatibility: changes are runtime-side only and transparent to the API; default behavior is conservative and gated behind a feature-flag for Dedicated/Private until rollout. Validation: unit and integration tests updated; new perf benchmarks added that reproduce customer workload shapes. Linked work: Linear ENG-2123, ENG-2199.

release_notes: Runtime: Improve streaming token latency by refactoring token loop, adaptive flush cadence, cooperative backpressure, KV-cache fast-path, and kernel scheduling heuristics. Default conservative behavior; feature-flagged rollout for Dedicated/Private.
perf_results: p50 token emission latency reduced ~18% and p95 reduced ~22% on 8k-seq interactive workloads; end-to-end observed streaming token delivery latency improved by median 120ms in our benchmark harness; continuous-batcher auto-tuner reduced per-token cost by ~6% without violating latency SLOs.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind runtime feature-flag 'streaming_latency_v2'. Rollout plan: enable in canary (10% Dedicated pods) for 48h, monitor token p95 and request error rates; fallback path available to revert to previous scheduler policy. Added logging hooks to trace flush decisions and backpressure events.
rationale: Multiple small sources combined to produce user-visible streaming lag. Single-change fixes had limited impact; coordinated changes across token loop, flush cadence, and cache hot-path provide measurable and stable improvements.
